chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: Why he made so few records and came home
summary: Smith left the big time and came home after about 18 years on the road, seeing little in recording and fearing for his health.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: If you had to explain why you made so few records, what
would you say would be the reason for that? Because you only made about a dozen sides, I think. Maybe a few more. But certainly less than a dozen on which you take solos.
Well, I left all the big deals. In other words, I left the big shots...
You mean, you moved out of New York.

Yeah, and came back South. I come on back home, and lay myself (?) right here. Back home I saw what it was all about. I didn't care about making records or nothing. After I got back home, I seen there wasn't too much in it. It was only for the bandleader at times, and you know, the average life of a musician in the limelight is about 17 years. I (?) come back, relaxing, do a little fishin' -- some of them even might live longer.
You mean, you were concerned to live even at that stage of your life?
You were a man of what? 35-40 years old?

Yeah. My family got dying out, so I thought I'd better come back home and stay with the rest of them before they all go leave me or I leave them. We need to enjoy each other. And I had been gone about 18 years. I left when I was young, I left home, and stayed away, and lived on the road and seen that I wasn't gainin' nothin' on the road.
